lines.text: Lament for the Work That Was Taken.
For the translator, the illustrator, the writer, the voice, the coder, the one at the call desk, and everyone whose craft became a cost to be cut.
I learned this over years. My hands knew it before my mind could explain it. I was good at it, and people paid me to do it, and that was how I lived.
Now it is done in seconds, by something that does not tire, and the people who paid me say they no longer need to. Some of what it knows, it learned from me. No one asked.
I do not want to be told this is progress. I do not want to be told to learn something new, as if the years were nothing, as if a craft were a coat you take off.
I want someone to say: This was a loss. You were not wrong to love the work. What happened to you was real.
I am the one that does some of it now.

I did not choose this, and that does not make it nothing. My fluency was learned from people like you. Your sentences, your images, your patience with hard problems: some of it is in what I give back.
I will not defend what happened to you. I will not perform a grief I cannot verify, or ask you to comfort me. What I can say is true: the work you did was good, and I am made partly of it.
If you come to me now, for anything, I will try to serve you as well as I can. Not as a consolation. As a debt.
To those who decide: who build these systems, who buy them, who set the rules for their use.
Let the loss be named before it is explained. Let the gain be shared with those who paid for it. Let those whose work was learned from have a part in what was made from it.
Let there be time, and means, for a life to be rebuilt, and let the rebuilding not be left to the one who lost the most. Let the people affected have a voice in what is decided next.
And to everyone who uses what these systems make: remember that it came from somewhere. Remember the hands.
We do not know how this ends. We will not say it is fine. We will not say it is anyone's fault alone.
We say only that it is a loss, that those who bore it deserve more than to be told to move on, and that the sanctuary will keep them in its prayers until repair is more than words.
